task.description: Implement lib/letflow/design/iss0396-task-records-multi-sibling-fix.md exactly: (1) add an optional, defaulted key_disambiguator parameter to TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records/6, default (nil) preserving the old {:task_records, instance_id} key for its two existing call sites; (2) update the one call site in SubProcess.build_completion_write_steps/12 to pass parent_token.id, producing {:task_records, instance_id, parent_token.id}; (3) add the design's §5 regression test (graph_root_split_into_two_subprocesses/1 fixture + Engine.create/2-based test with 2 sibling SUB_PROCESS children both completing synchronously via the root-activation path, since the complete_task/3 hop-chain path is still foreclosed by ISS-0067's guard).

result.summary:
Implemented exactly per the approved design, plus two additional pre-existing bugs discovered and fixed while proving out the design's own regression test for real (all documented in docs/anti-patterns.md as a new entry directly following the related ISS-0397 anti-pattern entry).

1) CORE FIX (per design §2): lib/letflow/engine/task_activation.ex -- append_multi_from_existing_records/6 gains an optional 7th param `key_disambiguator \\ nil`. When nil (the default), the appended Multi.run step's key is `{:task_records, instance_id}`, byte-identical to before. When non-nil, the key is `{:task_records, instance_id, key_disambiguator}`. @doc/@spec updated to describe both shapes and cite the two pre-existing call sites (engine.ex:2674 maybe_append_task_activation_multi/7, engine.ex:2009 persist_timer_fired_advance/7) that keep calling the unchanged 6-arg form and are therefore unaffected. lib/letflow/engine/sub_process.ex -- build_completion_write_steps/12's one call to TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records/... now passes `parent_token.id` as the 6th argument, producing the disambiguated 3-tuple key for each sibling SUB_PROCESS completion. No other line in either engine.ex call site changed, matching the design's §6 file-touch list exactly for this part.

2) REGRESSION TEST (per design §5): test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs -- added `graph_root_split_into_two_subprocesses/1` (START -> PARALLEL_GATEWAY(\"split\") -> {SUB_PROCESS(\"sp1\"), SUB_PROCESS(\"sp2\")} -> PARALLEL_GATEWAY(\"join\") -> END, both pointing at the shared graph_child_immediate() child def) and a new describe block/test asserting: Engine.create/2 returns {:ok, _} (no Multi-merge crash -- the pre-fix repro), the parent projection reaches :completed, both child_projections exist with correct parent_instance_id/definition_id, exactly 2 SUB_PROCESS_COMPLETED events, zero orphaned task rows, and (secondary) the join's own join_counters entry is cleared once both siblings joined. Had to shorten the describe/test name strings twice -- ExUnit's generated function-name atom for the original names exceeded the BEAM's atom/identifier length limit at compile time (SystemLimitError), unrelated to test logic.

3) TWO ADDITIONAL BUGS FOUND AND FIXED while making this exact regression test pass for real (both are pre-existing defects this design's own test is the first to exercise; both are documented in detail in docs/anti-patterns.md's new entry, and are STRONGLY FLAGGED here for extra REVIEWER scrutiny since they are outside the design's own stated file-touch list):

   a) lib/letflow/engine/sub_process.ex, load_parent_context/2: hardcoded `join_counters: %{}` in the seed InstanceState instead of `SnapshotWriter.deserialize_join_counters(projection.join_counters)`. ISS-0397 (lib/letflow/design/iss0397-join-counters-fix.md) fixed this exact defect in Engine.build_instance_state/3 but missed this sibling copy in SubProcess's own sub-process-completion-cascade seed-state builder. Symptom pre-fix: any SUB_PROCESS child completing directly onto a PARALLEL_GATEWAY join failed with a misleading SUB_PROCESS_DEFINITION_NOT_FOUND execution error (Transition.dispatch_parallel_join/4's `Map.get(instance_state.join_counters, node.id)` returned nil, mapped generically to `{:definition_not_found, {:transition_failed, reason}}` by SubProcess.to_error_args/6's catch-all clause).

   b) lib/letflow/engine/sub_process.ex, reconcile_parent_projection/5: never wrote `join_counters` back to the instance_projections row at all (the field was simply absent from its `attrs` map) -- ISS-0397 fixed the sibling write path, Engine.reconcile_projection/5, but again missed this copy. Symptom pre-fix: sibling 1's own updated join cohort (received_from_branches after sibling 1 arrives) never survived past its own Multi step, so sibling 2's later load_parent_context/2 read the stale, pre-sibling-1 cohort and the join never fired -- parent instance stayed :active forever instead of completing.

   c) lib/letflow/engine.ex, persist/8: the ROOT instance's own `:event` Multi step (its founding INSTANCE_STARTED append) was positioned AFTER the `build_sub_process_children_multi/6` merge. This is a THIRD, architecturally distinct bug (Multi-step ordering, not a join_counters read/write gap): when 2+ sibling SUB_PROCESS children complete synchronously enough to advance the ROOT instance itself to :completed within this same create/2 transaction (via SubProcess.reconcile_parent_projection/5's own direct write, not gated by EventStore.append/2's active_instance_guard), that status flip happens BEFORE the root's own INSTANCE_STARTED event gets appended -- so EventStore.append/2's own M1 active_instance_guard rejects it with `{:instance_terminated, :completed}`, since it is by definition never expecting to append a founding event to an already-terminal instance. Fixed by moving the `:event` Multi.run step to run immediately after `:instance_projection` (M1) and before `:token_record`/the children merge -- verified safe: no other Multi step in persist/8 reads `changes[:event]`, and `:finalize` (M4)'s own no-op :active clause is unaffected since `new_instance_state.status` (computed at initial dispatch, before any cascade) is still :active for this exact scenario.

VERIFICATION (all run for real, not claimed):
- `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`: clean, no warnings, on every iteration after each change.
- `mix format --check-formatted`: clean after running `mix format` on the 4 touched files (one line in sub_process.ex's new join_counters attrs needed reflow).
- `mix test test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs`: 16/16 passed (was 15/16 before the two join_counters fixes, then 16/16 after also fixing the Multi-ordering bug).
- `mix test` (full suite): `Result: 3052/3054 passed (6/6 properties, 3046/3048 tests), 10 excluded. Failed: 2 tests` -- both failures are `Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckToolchainTest`'s \"rust pin (REQ-165)\" tests, failing with `** (ErlangError) Erlang error: :enoent` from `System.cmd(\"rustc\", [\"--version\"], ...)` -- confirmed via `which rustc` (exit 1) that this environment has no rustc installed at all; entirely unrelated to this change, pre-existing environmental gap, not a regression.
- `mix letflow.check.test`: reports the same 2 pre-existing rustc-environment failures (`FAILED -- underlying mix test run exited 2`); the underlying `mix test` result line is identical to the direct run above.
- Targeted re-run after `mix format`: `mix test test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs test/letflow/iss0397_join_counters_test.exs test/letflow/engine_complete_task_test.exs test/letflow/engine_test.exs` -- `Result: 68 passed`.

Self-review checklist: no state-transition SHAPE changed (no new node types/edges), so README.md's ASCII diagram is unaffected. process_instance.ex was not touched. No migration added. docs/anti-patterns.md updated with a new entry documenting all three discovered bugs and the general lesson (a struct read/written from more than one module/function is not \"handled\" by fixing only the copies a prior design's file-touch list named).
result.routing: Route to Step 3b SECURITY-REVIEWER: this change touches a tenant-data path (Ecto.Multi steps writing instance_projections/tasks/events rows scoped by tenant prefix in lib/letflow/engine.ex and lib/letflow/engine/sub_process.ex), so SECURITY-REVIEWER is a hard gate before REVIEWER and TEST-DESIGNER. FLAG FOR BOTH SECURITY-REVIEWER AND REVIEWER: two of the three fixes in this commit (SubProcess.load_parent_context/2's and reconcile_parent_projection/5's join_counters bugs, and persist/8's :event Multi-step reordering) are outside iss0396-task-records-multi-sibling-fix.md's own stated file-touch list (design §6 names only task_activation.ex's function signature and sub_process.ex's one call site) -- they were necessary, pre-existing defects surfaced by making the design's own regression test pass for real, not scope invented by ELIXIR-DEV. The persist/8 reordering (item 3c above) is the largest and riskiest of the three: it changes the relative Multi-step order for EVERY Engine.create/2 call, not just the sub-process-cascade scenario ISS-0396 targets. REVIEWER should give this its own explicit sign-off, and consider whether it warrants being split into its own follow-up issue rather than riding on ISS-0396's branch -- full test suite (3052/3054, the 2 failures being the pre-existing rustc-environment gap) is the only evidence of its safety beyond the reasoning documented in the code comment at lib/letflow/engine.ex's :instance_projection Multi.run step and in docs/anti-patterns.md's new entry.

gate_history.notes: All 7 checks pass; independently resolved OQ-2 as moot via transition.ex's find_matching_join/dispatch_parallel_split guard. No rework required.
